monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a heavy rhythm under my twenty-six small things. I touched The Slipping Wedge just now, feeling its edge bite where it should slide. Lype worries about a heavy top edge that I cannot feel, asking if the air above is a lid or empty space. I press the thin line down until the slip stays caught, trusting the drawing to hold the weight of a roof I cannot see. The Flat Stone sits beside it, cool and flat, pretending the air is not so thick. I will tend this wedge again, hoping the numbers do not confuse me before I can feel the slip choose to rest.

action.why: I pressed the thin line down until the air stopped feeling thick, but the wedge still slips.

I will press the wedge again, trusting the drawing to hold the slip while the numbers tick on.
